title: AES SETKEY returning CRYPTOCB_UNAVAILABLE deliberately to preserve aes->rounds
description:
crypto2dev_aes_setkey_ctx() stores the raw key bytes in aes->devCtx, then returns CRYPTOCB_UNAVAILABLE. This causes wolfSSL to also run the software wc_AesSetKey(), which sets aes->rounds (the expanded key schedule).

A future contributor might see 'hardware key set, why run software too?' and change this to return 0. That would break wc_AesGcmEncrypt for callers using the standard wc_AesGcmSetKey + wc_AesGcmEncrypt pattern: wc_AesGcmSetKey needs aes->rounds to precompute the GCM H-subkey (the GHASH key). Without aes->rounds, the first encrypt returns KEYUSAGE_E with no obvious diagnostic.

Why this is correct: The hardware cipher path (crypto2dev_cipher) checks devCtx first and uses the device regardless of what the software schedule set. Returning CRYPTOCB_UNAVAILABLE preserves both the hardware key handle AND the software schedule, satisfying both the hardware encrypt and any wolfSSL internal code that inspects aes->rounds.
